item.title: Removing Boundary Smoothness from the Hot-Spots Conclusion in the Simple-Eigenvalue Case
item.description: arXiv:2610.12622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a reduction from a smooth-domain theorem excluding interior critical points of first positive Neumann eigenfunctions to a non-strict hot-spots conclusion on arbitrary bounded simply connected planar domains with compact Neumann resolvent and simple first positive eigenvalue. The main analytic step is spectral convergence under exhaustion by conformal images of concentric disks. A reflection extension, conformal invariance of Dirichlet energy, and compactness of the Sobolev embedding give a direct proof. A truncation argument justifies square integrability of the transferred extensions without any boundary regularity. The smooth-domain theorem proved by OpenAI is an external input; the approximation argument is proved here in full. The paper was generated by ChatGPT with prompts from the listed author.
item.dc:creator: Krzysztof Burdzy

item.title: A Framework for Arbitrary-Order Electromagnetic Field Approximation Based on Analytical Solutions of Maxwell's Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.12682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The standard Yee finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) algorithm uses Maxwell's equations to replace first order temporal derivatives with spatial curls. In this work, the relation is extended to arbitrary orders: a Time-Space Theorem establishes the correspondence between higher-order temporal derivatives and successively higher-order spatial curl operators. Based on this relation, an arbitrary-order framework for electromagnetic field approximations is developed. The framework constructs higher temporal orders through higher curl orders and permits different spatial discretizations and curl-estimation techniques, thereby providing a general basis for developing numerical algorithms of arbitrary orders. As one implementation, an arbitrary-order FDTD algorithm is constructed using staggered time and space stepping together with recursive curl estimations. Numerical simulations of an initial-value problem are performed for temporal approximation orders from second to tenth order while the spatial and temporal step sizes are kept fixed. Comparisons with the analytical solution show that the errors decrease rapidly and monotonically with increasing approximation order. These results demonstrate the practical potential of the framework for high-accuracy electromagnetic computation and provide a basis for further development of arbitrary-order numerical methods.
item.dc:creator: David Wei Ge

item.title: An exact Delaunay flux identity for compact equilibria in the liquid drop model
item.description: arXiv:2610.12689v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit the construction of compact liquid drop equilibria from Delaunay unduloids in [Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 249 (2025), Paper No. 74]. We evaluate exactly the coefficient arising in the final solvability condition of the Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction, identifying it as the product of the axial period and the normalised Delaunay flux. Using this identity and the monotonicity of the period, we establish the conjectured positivity of the coefficient and prove that its product with the period strictly increases with the neck radius. We also derive an exact relation between the volume and the surface area of one period and prove that both strictly decrease with the neck radius. These results extend the construction throughout the embedded unduloid family and yield compact equilibria of every sufficiently large mass, with reference neck radii converging to any prescribed interior value as the mass tends to infinity.
item.dc:creator: Averkios Averkiou, Manuel del Pino, Monica Musso

item.title: Stability threshold of the Couette flow in 2D Navier-Stokes Boussinesq equations on $\mathbb{T} \times [-1, 1]$ and $\mathbb{R} \times [-1, 1]$
item.description: arXiv:2610.12810v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the transition threshold problem for the 2D Navier-Stokes Boussinesq equations around the Couette flow with a constant background temperature in two domains: $\mathbb{T} \times [-1, 1]$ and $\mathbb{R} \times [-1, 1]$. It was proved that if the sizes of initial perturbations of the vorticity and the temperature in Sobolev spaces are $\nu^{\fr13}$ and $\nu^{\fr56}$, respectively, then this system admits a globally stable solution. Besides, we derive the enhanced dissipation estimate for the vorticity and temperature, as well as the inviscid damping estimate for the velocity. The coupling in the equations poses some difficulties to the analysis. We overcome these challenges and establish the results via the quasi-linear method and energy estimates.
item.dc:creator: Nangao Zhang, Gengwei Zhong, Ruizhao Zi

item.title: Precise propagation rates of the fractional Fisher-KPP equation with free boundaries
item.description: arXiv:2610.12838v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we determine the propagation rates of the Fisher-KPP equation with free boundaries and fractional diffusion $(-\Delta)^s$ $(0<s<1)$, which was considered in \cite{CDN26} as a model for species spreading, where the density function $u(t,x)$ satisfies the fractional Fisher-KPP equation $u_t+(-\Delta)^su=f(u)$ over a one-dimensional spatial domain $(g(t), h(t))$, representing the expanding population range, with $x=g(t)$ and $x=h(t)$ the free boundaries. It was shown in \cite{CDN26} that the model is well-posed, and its long-time dynamics exhibits a spreading-vanishing dichotomy. We show in this paper that, when spreading occurs, \[ \begin{cases} \lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{h(t)}{t^{1/(2s)}} =\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{-g(t)}{t^{1/(2s)}} =\left(\frac{2^{1-2s}\mu}{1-2s}\right)^{1/(2s)} & \mbox{ if $s\in(0,1/2)$,}\\[2mm] \lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{h(t)}{t\ln t} =\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{-g(t)}{t\ln t} =\mu & \mbox{ if $s=1/2$,}\\[2mm] \lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{h(t)}{t} =\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{-g(t)}{t} =c_0(s) & \mbox{ if $s\in(1/2,1)$}, \end{cases} \] where $c_0(s)\in (0,\infty)$ is uniquely determined by the associated semi-wave problem. The level sets of $u(t,x)$ propagate with the same rates as the free boundaries. The proof uses delicate upper and lower solutions constructed from a smooth profile function in the case $s\in (0, 1/2]$, and from the semi-wave profile when $s\in (1/2, 1)$.
item.dc:creator: Huyuan Chen, Yihong Du, Wenjie Ni

item.title: Global Well-Posedness and Energy Decay for an Abstract Viscoelastic Wave Equation with Nonlocal or Friction Damping
item.description: arXiv:2610.12846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates an abstract viscoelastic wave equation in a separable Hilbert space, in which the damping term depends on a power of the velocity norm. Depending on whether the power exponent is zero or nonzero, this damping corresponds to friction damping or nonlocal damping, respectively; the equation also contains a viscoelastic damping represented by an integral term with a relaxation function. We establish global well-posedness for initial data in \(\mathcal{H}_1\) by combining monotone operator theory with the Faedo--Galerkin method, and prove uniqueness for all exponents greater than \(-1\), with the singular range between \(-1\) and \(0\) handled through the monotonicity rather than the Lipschitz continuity of the nonlocal damping operator. We then study the long-time behavior of the energy via integral inequalities, multiplier techniques, and Nakao's method, and obtain explicit decay estimates showing that the energy decays exponentially in the friction case and polynomially in the nonlocal case. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to consider the combined effects of viscoelastic damping and nonlocal damping in such an abstract framework, and it is also the first to analyze nonlocal damping with negative exponents.
item.dc:creator: Jun Zhou, Teng Wang

item.title: Localized Generative Design of Ship Hulls with Diffusion Models and High-Fidelity Assessment
item.description: arXiv:2610.12870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Practical ship design requires localized refinement and performance evaluation. This paper presents a reward-directed diffusion framework for localized hull optimization. Parametric masking during dataset generation restricts geometric changes to selected variables, including the bulbous bow and forebody, while preserving full-hull continuity. Surrogate-assisted sequential Monte Carlo sampling targets reduced predicted calm-water resistance, with stability retained through training data and displacement matched during screening. An automated viscous free-surface CFD pipeline, validated against measurements for two benchmark container ships, evaluates a generated variant and GenHull E, a hull refined by a naval architect within the same representation. At matched KRISO Container Ship (KCS) displacement, the generated variant has comparable total resistance at $F_n=0.195$ but 45-50% higher resistance at $F_n=0.250$ and $0.260$, missed by empirical screening. GenHull E achieves 6-8% lower total resistance up to $F_n=0.240$ but higher resistance above $F_n=0.250$ as opposing friction and pressure trends reverse the gains. Aggregating resistance across this crossover can conceal tradeoffs that emerge when friction and pressure components are evaluated separately. The assessment reveals an inability to represent a faired bulbous bow and a reward lacking viscous pressure and stability terms. These findings show how high-fidelity assessment informs improved representations and objectives for physically realizable generative designs.
item.dc:creator: Hadi Keramati, Mohammed A. Hannan, Patrick Kirchen, Sina Tousi, Joonas Riekkinen, Jim Pyra, Rajeev K. Jaiman

item.title: Fourier--Laplace Injectivity for Oblique and Polygonal Cylinders in Passive Inverse Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.12983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Fourier--Laplace transforms on null phases arising in passive inverse problems. Densities with codimension-one dependence in oblique cylinders are first considered. Integration in the distinguished direction reduces the data to an entire transform on a real-analytic maximally totally real submanifold. Holomorphic uniqueness then gives injectivity. A fixed transverse polytope swept along a polygonal curve, forming a polygonal cylinder, is next considered. The density is assumed to be polynomial in the material transverse variables on each swept piece. A weighted Brion--Barvinok expansion separates the vertex terms and the successive pieces. The same representation gives a finite-dimensional Lipschitz estimate when the polynomial degree is fixed. We apply these transform results to passive wave and heat equations in arbitrary dimension. The initial state is zero outside the observation domain. Equality of the Laplace-domain boundary data determines the quantity of the initial data divided by the speed squared in the acoustic model and the quantity of the initial data divided by the coefficient of thermal conductivity in the parabolic model. The question of what remains true when only weighted generalized boundary data on a finite interval \([0,T]\) are available is then studied. These data determine the harmonic moments of the quotient up to the weighted terminal residual. This identity gives a H\"older estimate in an oblique cylinder and a Lipschitz estimate in a polygonal cylinder. Finally, a continuous generating curve is approximated by a polygonal curve and a continuous material density by piecewise transverse polynomials. The resulting reconstruction estimate separates measurement noise, density approximation error, geometric error, and the condition number of the finite sampling matrix.
item.dc:creator: Yan Jiang, Hongyu Liu, Tianhao Ni, Kai Zhang

item.title: Sharp Sobolev inequalities on minimal immersions via optimal transport
item.description: arXiv:2610.13052v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that, for $2\leq p<n$, the optimal $L^p$-Sobolev constant on every complete $n$-dimensional Euclidean minimal immersion without boundary is the Euclidean Aubin--Talenti constant. The proof combines optimal transport to a suitably chosen target with a two-kernel comparison linking the tangential transport moment to deficits in the normal-fibre and Jacobian estimates.
item.dc:creator: Zhe-Feng Xu, Zhuo-Nan Zhu

item.title: Qualitative-to-quantitative regularity for degenerate equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.13137v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a principle that converts qualitative regularity into uniform interior estimates for degenerate equations. For the $p$-Laplace equation, $p>2$, we prove that local $C^{1,\gamma}$ regularity of every solution, without any uniform bound on the corresponding seminorms, implies uniform $C^{1,\beta}$ estimates for every $0<\beta<\gamma$. Thus, the optimal qualitative and quantitative gradient H\"older exponents coincide as suprema in every dimension. In the plane, this yields estimates controlled by the $L^p$ norm of the solution for every exponent below the sharp Iwaniec--Manfredi threshold. Applied to Xu's recent qualitative $C^{1,1/3}$ regularity for planar infinity-harmonic functions, we obtain uniform interior $C^{1,\beta}$ estimates for every $0<\beta<1/3$. For the nonlocal superconductivity equation $|Du|(-\Delta)^s u=0$, with $1/2<s<1$, we prove that pointwise differentiability of all solutions with integrable tails implies uniform interior $C^{1,\alpha}$ estimates for bounded solutions, for some $\alpha>0$. The proofs combine compactness for shifted equations with an improvement-of-flatness iteration at variable scales.
item.dc:creator: Aelson Sobral, Eduardo V. Teixeira, Jos\'e Miguel Urbano

item.title: Strict Dirichlet P\'olya Inequality for Simply Connected Planar Domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.13139v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the strict Dirichlet P\'olya inequality on every bounded simply connected planar domain. The proof uses a unitary boundary transport formulation of the Helmholtz equation and relates Dirichlet resonances to unitary eigenphase crossings through the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. An exact area identity yields the sharp Weyl coefficient, while a Ky Fan estimate leaves a strictly positive remainder in the counting estimate. The general case follows by conformal exhaustion.
item.dc:creator: Quanyu Tang, Zuoqin Wang

item.title: Remarks on temperature-dependent Cahn--Hilliard equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.13140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We recall several derivations of temperature-dependent Cahn-Hilliard equations. The resulting equations are systems of mixed order. For a suitable subclass of equations we discuss its local-in-time well-posedness based on $L^p$-maximal regularity theory. We also discuss stability of equilibria.
item.dc:creator: Mi-Ho Giga, Yoshikazu Giga, Naoto Kajiwara, Kazuyuki Tsuda

item.title: Stability of composite waves consisting of a non-classical Liu shock and a rarefaction wave for a non-convex viscoelastic system
item.description: arXiv:2610.13151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the time-asymptotic stability of composite waves consisting of a non-classical Liu shock and a rarefaction wave for non-convex viscoelastic system. By choosing delicate time-dependent shift functions to the viscous shock and suitable weight functions for the relative entropy, we succeed in proving the time-asymptotic stability of the composite of a viscous Liu shock and a rarefaction wave from two different characteristic families for the one-dimensional viscoelastic system with a cubic non-convex stress-strain relation by $a$-contraction method. Here the non-classical Liu shock can be either degenerate or non-degenerate, which can be seen as the system version of the scalar Oleinik shock. Note that both the shift and the weight functions are chosen quite differently in the two cases of nearly degenerate and fully non-degenerate. The paper represents the first time-asymptotic stability result for the composite waves consisting of both non-classical Liu shock and rarefaction wave from two different families for the non-convex physical system.
item.dc:creator: Feimin Huang, Yi Wang, Jian Zhang

item.title: Minimizing tangent maps into complex projective space
item.description: arXiv:2610.13214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify all nonconstant smooth harmonic maps $\mathbb{S}^2\to \mathbb{CP}^n$ and $\mathbb{S}^3\to \mathbb{CP}^n$ whose 0-homogeneous extensions are minimizing: they are, respectively, isometric embeddings or holomorphic isometric embeddings composed with a Hopf map.
item.dc:creator: Matilde Gianocca, Andr\'e Guerra, David Ziener

item.title: Gradient rearrangement estimates for singular and degenerate anisotropic $p$-Laplace equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.13226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove global pointwise estimates on the decreasing rearrangement \(u^{\ast}\) and \([H(\nabla u)]^{\ast}\) of SOLAs \(u\) of an elliptic Poisson equation driven by the anisotropic \(p\)-Laplace operator \(\Delta_p^H\) for given \(L^1\)-data and equipped with either homogeneous Dirichlet or Neumann boundary conditions. Here, we assume that the dimension \(n\ge 2\), \(1<p<n\) and \(H\) is norm on \(\R^n\). In the degenerate range \(2 \leq p <n\), this gives an anisotropic extension and a full-interval completion of the rearrangement theory of Cianchi-Maz'ya [JEMS, 2014]. In particular, we obtain a new rearrangement estimate for gradients by decomposing the data for singular range \(1<p<2\), where the nonlinear interpolation method aren't available. Moreover, the endpoint weak-type gradient estimate is obtained for all \(1<p<n\). In the range \(p_*(n)<p<n\) with \(p_*(n):=\frac{3n-2}{2n-1}\), we prove a stability estimate for differences of gradients. These results extends the known ones in the literature to the singular range \(p_*(n)<p<2\).
item.dc:creator: Lu Chen, Daniel Hauer, Yabo Yang

item.title: Vector and matrix monotonicity characterisation of the "load forces" in nonlinear elasticity: compressible versus incompressible response
item.description: arXiv:2610.13235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the relation between different notions of monotonicity for isotropic hyperelastic compressible and incompressible materials. We study how to define the monotonicity concept on the manifold $\rm{Sym}^{++}(n)\cap \rm{SL}(n)$ of positive definite symmetric tensors with unit determinant and the corresponding spectral manifold $\mathcal S=\left\{(\lambda_1,\dotsc,\lambda_n)\in \mathbb{R}^n_+\,\middle|\, \lambda_1\lambda_2\cdots\lambda_n=1\right\}$, and give a precise characterisation of monotonicity in the case of hyperelastic materials. In particular, we consider the monotonicity properties of the Biot stress tensor $T_{\rm Biot}(U)$, the engineering stress, or the load tensor.
item.dc:creator: Jendrik Voss, Ionel-Dumitrel Ghiba, Robert J. Martin, Patrizio Neff

item.title: Weighted derivative estimates for Kolmogorov equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.13241v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For diffusions whose coefficients are smooth, with at most linear growth and bounded derivatives of higher order, we establish explicit pointwise bounds on the spatial derivatives of the classical solution to the Cauchy problem with polynomially growing initial data. We also obtain explicit growth estimates for the derivatives of the SDE with respect to the initial data. The proofs combine Lyapunov functions and Markov semigroups on weighted spaces with Kunita's theory of the differentiable dependence of SDE solutions on the initial data.
item.dc:creator: Artur Sidorenko, Vasilii Kolokoltsov

item.title: Global Regular Solutions for One-Dimensional Degenerate Compressible Non-Resistive MHD Equations with Large Data and Far-Field Vacuum
item.description: arXiv:2610.13248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem on the real line for a one-dimensional transverse-field isentropic non-resistive magnetohydrodynamic system with viscosity $\mu(\rho)=\alpha\rho^\delta$, $0<\delta\leq1$, and vacuum at spatial infinity. The viscosity therefore vanishes precisely where the density vanishes. We establish two global large-data theorems, one for the sublinear range $0<\delta<1$ and one for the linear case $\delta=1$, in a nontrivial invariant class of magnetic fields. The class is described by the frozen-in flux $h=b/\rho$ and its mass derivative $k=\rho^{-1}h_x$. The key identity $[\partial_t+u\partial_x,\rho^{-1}\partial_x]=0$ transports both $h$ and $k$, removes all negative powers of the density from the Lorentz force, and propagates the magnetic regularity. A modified effective-velocity entropy contains an additional coercive magnetic term, while its only error is controlled by $k$. Magnetic pressure also strengthens the density upper bound. These estimates close the large-data continuation argument in the ranges $0<\delta<1$, $\gamma\geq\delta+\tfrac12$, and $\delta=1$, $\gamma>\tfrac32$. As a result, we extend the work of Cao, Li, and Zhu (SIAM J. Math. Anal., 2022) from the Navier-Stokes equations to the MHD equations.
item.dc:creator: Zhaoyang Shang

item.title: Loss of derivatives for hyperbolic operators with coefficients oscillating in time
item.description: arXiv:2610.13343v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider second-order strictly hyperbolic operators whose coefficients are Lipschitz continuous in space and may oscillate near the initial time. Their first two time derivatives are bounded by the corresponding powers of $\frac{1}{t}(\log\frac{1}{t})^\alpha$ with $0\leqslant\alpha<1$, and the first time derivative satisfies the corresponding spatial Lipschitz bound. By combining Tarama's energy with frequency-dependent weights, we prove an energy estimate without loss for $\alpha=0$ and with a stretched logarithmic upper bound for the loss when $0<\alpha<1$, which implies an arbitrarily small loss in the Sobolev scale. These estimates extend the analysis of Colombini, Del Santo and Fanelli [\emph{Ann. Scuola Norm. Sup. Pisa Cl. Sci. (5)} \textbf{26} (2025)] for spatially Lipschitz coefficients to time-derivative bounds with an additional logarithmic factor.
item.dc:creator: Wenhui Chen, Michael Reissig

item.title: Complex Monge-Amp{\`e}re equations with boundary values: a variational approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.13478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Omega$ ___ C n be a bounded hyperconvex domain and $\Phi$\,: $\Omega$ $\rightarrow$ R a maximal plurisubharmonic function in $\Omega$ (possibly unbounded). We introduce a new class E 1 $\Phi$ ($\Omega$) of plurisubharmonic functions with boundary values equal to $\Phi$ in the sense of Cegrell and finite $\Phi$-energy on $\Omega$. Then given a Borel measure $\mu$ on $\Omega$, we apply a variational approach to prove that $\mu$ is the Monge-Amp{\`e}re measure of a function u $\in$ E 1 $\Phi$ ($\Omega$) if and only if it satisfies the integrability condition We also establish a quantitative version of this condition extending previous results of Cegrell and others. Using a logarithmic transformation, we obtain analogous results for the real Monge-Amp{\`e}re equations with (unbounded) boundary data.
item.dc:creator: Papa Badiane (UASZ), Chinh H. Lu (LAREMA), Souhaibou Sambou (UFR SAT), Ahmed Zeriahi (IMT)

item.title: Weighted Liouville Theorems and A Priori Bounds for Indefinite Superlinear Equations with Pucci's Maximal Operator
item.description: arXiv:2610.13486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider \begin{equation*}\ \left\{ \begin{aligned} -\mathcal_{\lambda,\Lambda}^{+}(D^{2}u)&=\mu u+a(x)u^{p}\quad\text{in}~\Omega,\\ u&=0\quad\text{on}~~\partial\Omega, \end{aligned} \right. \end{equation*} where $ \ Omega$ is a smooth bounded domain, $a$ is a continuous function which is allowed to change sign. Moreover, the set of zeros of $a$ may have a non-empty interior. The main objective of this article is to establish a uniform bound on the set of positive solutions of the above problem. This approach requires a suitable Liouville-type theorem. We first prove the Liouville-type theorem for $-\mathcal_{\lambda,\Lambda}^{+}(D^{2}v)=h(x_{1})f(v),$ where \(h\) is a strictly increasing one-dimensional weight and \(f\) is positive and nondecreasing.
item.dc:creator: Karan Rathore, Mohan Mallick, Ram Baran Verma

item.title: Blocking of bistable front propagation: Application to Wolbachia population replacement
item.description: arXiv:2610.13497v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In order to control epidemics of mosquito-borne diseases such as dengue, for which there is still no vaccine available, several strategies aim to directly target the mosquito population. One technique involves introducing a symbiotic bacterium called Wolbachia into the population, which blocks the transmission of pathogens. A mathematical model of the introduction of this bacterium and the replacement of the mosquito population with a population carrying this bacterium has been developed, proving that in a homogeneous environment, there is spatial propagation of the replacement. The objective of this paper is to study the blocking of this propagation in cases where the environment is not homogeneous. In particular, we are considering scenarios where the environmental carrying capacity varies significantly across different regions of the spatial domain. To achieve this objective, we first reduce the original 2x2 reaction-diffusion system to a single closed equation, providing a simplified framework for studying the dynamics of Wolbachia propagation. We then investigate the blocking of the propagation in the population replacement process, focusing on the effects of spatial variations in the environmental carrying capacity. Numerical simulations have been performed to validate the theoretical results.
item.dc:creator: Saoussen Latrach (LAGA), Nicolas Vauchelet (LAGA), Hatem Zaag (LAGA)

item.title: Short scale asymptotics in nonlocal spectral problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.13513v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of eigenvalues of nonlocal convolution-type operators $$L_\varepsilon\rho=-\frac{1}{\varepsilon^{d}}\int_\Omega J\left({\frac{|x-y|^2}{\varepsilon^2}}\right)\rho(y)dy+a(x)\rho(x),$$ (with a continuous sufficiently fast decaying at infinity function $J\geq 0$) when the scaling parameter $\varepsilon>0$ tends to zero. Assuming that the minimum of the function $a(x)$ is attained at a point $x_0\in \overline{\Omega}\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ and is non-degenerate, we establish several terms in the asymptotic expansion of the first eigenvalues $\lambda_\varepsilon^{(k)}$ of $L_\varepsilon$. If $x_0$ is an interior point of the domain $\Omega$, we show that $\lambda_\varepsilon^{(k)}=a(x_0)-1+\varepsilon\mu^{(k)}+\overline{o}(\varepsilon)$, where $\mu^{(k)}$ are eigenvalues of a harmonic oscillator (obtained by the blow up analysis), the corresponding eigenfunctions of $\mathcal{L}_\varepsilon$ are concentrated near $x_0$ on the scale $\varepsilon^{1/2}$. If $x_0\in\partial \Omega$ then the asymptotic expansion of the eigenvalues of $L_\varepsilon$ has the form $\lambda_\varepsilon^{(k)}=a(x_0)-1+\varepsilon^{2/3}\Lambda_0+\varepsilon(\mu^{(k)}+\alpha p_0)+\overline{o}(\varepsilon)$. The corresponding eigenfunctions are represented as the product of a function depending on the distance to $\partial\Omega$ and concentrated on the scale $\varepsilon^{2/3}$, and functions localized on the scale $\varepsilon^{1/2}$ and asymptotically independent of the distance to $\partial\Omega$. The latter functions converge (after rescaling) to eigenfunctions of a harmonic oscillator (in tangential variables), $\mu^{(k)}$ being their eigenvalues. The former function is given, to the leading term, by the scaled Airy function, and $\Lambda_0$, $\alpha$ and $p_0$ depend on $J(|x|^2)$ and $a(x)$.
item.dc:creator: Volodymyr Rybalko, Antonina Rybalko

item.title: H\"{o}lder regularity of solutions to parabolic equations associated with fractional $p$-Laplacian type operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.13539v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study H\"{o}lder regularity of local weak super-solutions to the parabolic equation associated with fractional $p$-Laplacian type operators $$ \partial_t u(t,x)-\text{p.v.}\int_{\R^d}|u(t,y)-u(t,x)|^{p-2}(u(t,y)-u(t,x))J(t;x,y)\,dy=0,\quad (t,x)\in \R\times \R^d, $$ where $\text{p.v.}$ denotes the principal value, $p\in(1,\infty)$ and the kernel $J(t;x,y)$ is comparable (uniformly with respect to $(t;x,y)\in\R\times\R^d\times\R^d$) to the fractional $p$-Laplacian kernel $|x-y|^{-d-sp}$ with $s\in(0,1)$. Our contribution extends the fundamental work of Kassmann and Weidner to the nonlinear case $p\ne 2$. In particular, we provide an explicit nonlocal parabolic tail condition in terms of an $L^{1+\varepsilon}$-norm in the time variable (for a suitable $\varepsilon>0$) for all $p\in(1,\infty)$, under which H\"older regularity holds. Our proof is based on the method of expansion of positivity, which is the key ingredient in the reduction-of-oscillation argument.
item.dc:creator: Takashi Kumagai, Jian Wang, Meng-ge Zhang

item.title: Identifying secondary critical mass levels in two- and higher-dimensional Keller-Segel systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.13559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The parabolic-elliptic Keller-Segel system \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} u_t = \Delta u - \nabla \cdot (u\nabla v), \\[1mm] 0 = \Delta v - \mu + u, \qquad \mu:=\frac{1}{|\Omega|} \int_\Omega u, \end{array} \right. \qquad \qquad (\star) \] is considered under homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions in the ball $\Omega=B_R(0)\subset {\mathbb R}^n$, where $n\ge 2$ and $R>0$. The main results identify a mass level $m_\star(n,R)>0$ as critical in the sense that $\bullet$ whenever $0<m<m_\star(n,R)$, the constant equilibrium of ($\star$) given by $u\equiv v\equiv \frac{m}{|B_R|}$ is locally asymptotically stable with respect to the norm in $L^\infty(B_R)$, but that $\bullet$ if $m>m_\star(n,R)$, then any solution of ($\star$) emanating from nonnegative and nonconstant continuous radial initial data $u_0$ with $\int_{B_R} u_0=m$ and $\frac{1}{|B_r|} \int_{B_r} u_0 \ge \frac{m}{|B_R|}$ for all $r\in (0,R)$ blows up in finite time. The value of $m_\star(n,R)$ can be determined in an essentially explicit manner in dependence on principal zeroes of appropriate Bessel functions of the first kind; in particular, $m_\star(2,R)\approx 14.68197 \cdot \pi$ for all $R>0$. Accordingly, as a supplement to known mass-dependent blow-up dichotomies these findings reveal a genuinely secondary critical mass phenomenon for ($\star$) especially also in its two-dimensional version in which no precedent of this form seems known.
item.dc:creator: Yulan Wang, Michael Winkler

item.title: Boundary stabilization of multi-dimensional first-order quasilinear hyperbolic systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.13577v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the long-time behaviour of multi-dimensional first-order symmetrizable quasilinear hyperbolic systems with nonlinear feedback boundary conditions. Assuming strict interior and boundary Lyapunov inequalities for the linearized system and non-characteristic boundaries, we prove global existence for small initial data and exponential H^s decay, with s>d/2+1 an integer. We consider both bounded smooth domains and flat periodic cylinders, and illustrate the results with physical examples and numerical simulations.
item.dc:creator: Haitian Yang

item.title: The conformal Poisson embedding method for the anisotropic Calder\'on problem with a potential
item.description: arXiv:2610.13592v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the local Dirichlet-to-Neumann map of $\Delta_g+q$ determines a compact connected real-analytic Riemannian manifold of dimension at least three and a real-analytic real-valued potential, up to a diffeomorphism fixing the observed boundary and the conformal gauge of the equation. The result is new even when \(q\) is constant, i.e. for the fixed-frequency (Helmholtz) equation \(\Delta_g u+\lambda u=0\). The measurements are restricted to an arbitrary nonempty open boundary set $\Gamma$. The proof develops conformal Poisson embeddings method and uses coordinates given by quotients of solutions.
item.dc:creator: C\u{a}t\u{a}lin I. C\^arstea, Tony Liimatainen, Yi-Hsuan Lin, William Trad

item.title: Global Existence and Partial Regularity for the Three-Dimensional Chemotaxis--Navier--Stokes System in a Half-Space
item.description: arXiv:2610.13613v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish endpoint partial regularity for suitable weak solutions to the three-dimensional chemotaxis--Navier--Stokes system with constant sensitivity and linear consumption in a half-space under no-slip and no-flux boundary conditions. The full space--time singular set, including its boundary part, has vanishing one-dimensional parabolic Hausdorff measure. This follows from a Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg type criterion at the natural $r^{-1}$ dissipation scaling, valid at interior and boundary points without additional pressure smallness. The key estimate combines weighted mass control with the localized entropy--energy inequality to close the iteration without a separate $n\log n$ quantity and accounts for the mass term generated by rescaling. Boundary-compatible pressure and caloric decompositions yield local H\"older regularity. We also prove a lower-order criterion requiring smallness only of the velocity, signal gradient, and pressure oscillation, with a threshold depending on an arbitrary finite density mass bound. We construct global suitable weak solutions under natural entropy and energy assumptions without smallness restrictions on the initial data. The potential is time-independent with bounded gradient; boundedness of the potential itself is assumed only for the large-time results. If its gradient is also H\"older continuous, a solution can be selected to become bounded and classical throughout the closed half-space after a finite waiting time. For the same solution, we obtain decay and Neumann Gaussian asymptotics for both scalar components without initial spatial moment assumptions. The profile coefficients are the conserved bacterial mass and the limiting signal mass, respectively, and the latter is strictly positive whenever the initial signal is nonzero.
item.dc:creator: Yubo Chen, Jianbo Yu

item.title: Global Existence of Strong and Weak Solutions to the 2D Compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson System in Bounded Domains with Large Data and Vacuum
item.description: arXiv:2610.13618v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the two-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson system in a general simply connected bounded domain with Navier-slip boundary conditions and a positive, possibly non-flat, doping profile. We establish the global existence of a unique strong solution and of a global weak solution for arbitrarily large initial data allowing vacuum when the shear viscosity is a positive constant and the bulk one proportional to a power of the density with the power bigger than 4/3. The main difficulties arise from the interaction between the Poisson force and the general boundary geometry. To overcome them, we introduce a modified material derivative and derive quantitative $L^p$ estimates for the density by means of a Neumann duality argument together with a harmonic correction generated by the Navier-slip boundary condition. We further obtain a pointwise representation of the effective viscous flux by pulling back the Neumann Green function on the unit disk through a conformal mapping. The resulting commutator estimates, combined with elliptic estimates for the Poisson equation, yield a uniform-in-time upper bound for the density and allow us to close the higher-order a priori estimates. Finally, the global weak solution is constructed through a charge-preserving approximation and compactness argument.
item.dc:creator: Yingzhi Du, Huijiang Zhao

item.title: An inverse spectral problem for the wave equation with a varying Robin parameter at the boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.13629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An inverse spectral problem for a $(1+1)$-dimensional wave equation with wave speed $c(x)$ is considered. The spectral data consist of the eigenvalues of the Neumann--Dirichlet problem for the operator $-c^2(x)\partial_x^2$ together with their derivatives with respect to a Robin parameter at the boundary. We propose a two-step recovery procedure. In the first step, the Neumann-to-Dirichlet map $\Lambda$ is reconstructed from the spectral data using the results of arXiv/0406582. In the second step, the reconstructed $\Lambda$ is used within the regularization strategy for the boundary control method presented in arXiv:1509.04478. As an improvement, the regularization of the control problems employs a weighted combination of $L^2$ and $H^1$ penalty terms, and we prove a uniform convergence result for the family of optimal controls, thereby allowing the regularization parameters to be tuned simultaneously. We also prove that the forward spectral map, which assigns to a wave speed its spectral data, is Lipschitz continuous, and that the inverse spectral map underlying the reconstruction procedure is H\"older continuous on a subclass of wave speeds. The method is implemented numerically and validated on both smooth and piecewise smooth wave speed profiles. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the recovery of the wave speed exhibits high accuracy and robustness.
item.dc:creator: Antti Hannukainen, Petr Kulikov, Matti Lassas, Lauri Oksanen

item.title: Diffraction of waves by finite thin coatings: asymptotic expansion and effective models
item.description: arXiv:2610.13680v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the Helmholtz equation in a Dirichlet angular sector (which may be locally perturbed) covered on one side by a thin homogeneous layer. First, we propose an asymptotic expansion of the solution at any order and for any angle when the thickness of the layer tends to 0, using a matched asymptotic expansion. This consists in introducing different asymptotic expansions in three subdomains -- the vicinity of the corner, the layer and the rest of the domain -- that are linked through matching conditions. The presence of the corner makes these matching conditions delicate to derive because the fields have complex singular behaviors. We overcome this difficulty using a novel system of algebraic tools, including formal series and operators on these series. Moreover, we justify the asymptotic expansion with error estimates and provide details on the form of the expansion depending on the angle. We numerically validate this expansion up to order 5. This requires computing the behavior at infinity of some corner profiles. To do this, we introduce a Galerkin-type method enriched by complements at infinity. These complements are known functions that appear in the behavior at infinity of the corner profiles with coefficients that become unknowns of the system. Finally, we propose effective models of order 3, resp. 5 where, far from the corner, the layer is replaced with an effective Robin, resp. Ventcel, boundary condition and, near the corner, an artificial boundary is introduced and a Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) type condition is imposed. The DtN map relies on a modal decomposition of the truncated asymptotic expansion at order 3, resp. 5. The modes take into account the singular behavior of the expansion terms, the corner profiles and some algebraic matching coefficients. We prove the well-posedness of our effective models, as well as error estimates, and provide numerical results.
item.dc:creator: C\'edric Baudet

item.title: Travel time tomography for elliptically anisotropic elastic planar media
item.description: arXiv:2610.13747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the gauge of the travel time tomography problem for elliptically anisotropic planar media. Under this assumption the respective slowness surfaces consist of an inner ellipse and an outer circle. Hence, the singularities of seismic waves propagate on geodesics given by two Riemannian metrics of which the one related to shear waves is conformally Euclidean. We show that if both of these metrics are lens rigid then, up to boundary fixing diffeomorphisms, each elliptically anisotropic stiffness tensor is uniquely determined by the lens data whenever it has at least one isotropic point. If none of those points exists, then there are exactly two elliptically anisotropic stiffness tensors with the same lens data. Clearly, not all boundary fixing diffeomorphisms preserve the imposed structure of the slowness surface. We show that the set of well-behaved diffeomorphisms is never a subgroup of all boundary fixing diffeomorphisms. Our proofs are based on an interplay of algebra and geometry, and the key of the proofs is a characterization of the elliptic anisotropy via several polynomial conditions.
item.dc:creator: Joonas Ilmavirta, Teemu Saksala, Hj{\o}rdis Schl\"uter

item.title: Asymmetric minimal mass blow-up for the quintic NLS on a star graph
item.description: arXiv:2610.13752v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work is concerned with the focusing quintic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on a star graph with two edges, with a delta interaction of arbitrary strength at the vertex. We construct a non-radial, minimal mass, finite time blow-up solution, whose singularity forms at an arbitrarily prescribed interior point of one edge. Our approach is based on a suitable cut-off of the standard pseudoconformal blow-up solution of the focusing quintic NLS on the line, inspired by Ogawa-Tsutsumi and Burq-G\'erard-Tzvetkov. A noteworthy feature of our construction is the persistence of the domain of the Hamiltonian under the flow, obtained by the persistence of regularity method of Kato. We also identify a two-parameter family of distinct blow-up profiles, which should play a central role in the classification of non-radial minimal mass blow-up solutions on the star graph. Our construction is generic and can be extended to a star graph with an arbitrary number of edges. It can certainly also be adapted to other types of metric graphs.
item.dc:creator: Mattia Buratti, Fran\c{c}ois Genoud, Vladimir Georgiev

item.title: Scattering for the KP-II equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.13753v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove scattering in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$ for real-valued solutions of the KP-II equation with localized initial data. The hypotheses cover all Schwartz functions, data with a half spatial moment in $B^2_{1,1}$, and a class of weighted tensor Besov spaces allowing low regularity in either coordinate. The proof uses the scalar $\bar\partial$ equation associated with the heat operator. A uniform inverse estimate and an exact $L^2$ identity give an inverse construction for large amplitudes. We then estimate the nonlinear remainder on the propagation cones of free solutions and identify the limiting spectral mass through the heat equation. No smallness or zero horizontal mean condition is required. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first result establishing scattering for the KP-II equation for every real-valued Schwartz initial datum.
item.dc:creator: Xi Chen

item.title: Existence and uniqueness of bound states with prescribed number of nodes for nonlinear dispersive equations on spherically symmetric manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.13813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Standing waves $e^{i\omega t}u(x)$ of nonlinear dispersive equations, such as the nonlinear Schr\"odinger and Klein--Gordon equations, have a profile $u$ that solves a nonlinear elliptic ODE of the form $\Delta u+f(u)=0$. We prove the existence of radial bound states with a prescribed number of nodal surfaces for this equation, on a large class of spherically symmetric manifolds and nonlinearities $f$. Under mild assumptions, we prove uniqueness of such bound states for the model nonlinearity $f(u)=|u|^{p-1}u-u$. Both existence and uniqueness results apply to some manifolds with a singularity at the origin.
item.dc:creator: Valentino Badalucco

item.title: Existence and large-field asymptotics of Hopfions in a continuum model of frustrated magnets
item.description: arXiv:2610.13883v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a continuum model of frustrated magnetism that supports particle-like field configurations with nontrivial Hopf index. The energy functional combines competing second and first order exchange interactions with a stabilizing external magnetic field and gives rise to a variational problem for maps from three-dimensional space into the two-sphere. We prove the existence of energy minimizers in infinitely many nontrivial homotopy classes. We further establish the existence of a unit-charge Hopfion in the regime of strong external fields. Finally, we analyze the corresponding large-field limit, identify the natural concentration scale, and prove strong convergence of suitably rescaled minimizers to a minimizer of a limiting variational problem.
item.dc:creator: Glal Bacho, Christof Melcher

item.title: Ground states and sharp logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for logarithmic Schr\"odinger equations with partial confinement
item.description: arXiv:2610.13887v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the logarithmic Schr\"odinger equation with an arbitrary positive semidefinite quadratic potential and a periodic potential in the unconfined directions. The main variational difficulty is to turn a constrained minimizer into a critical point when the energy is extended-valued and not of class $C^1$ on the natural Hilbert space. We establish an abstract principle for convex lower semicontinuous energies with a smooth perturbation, allowing a scaling law for the full energy without requiring homogeneity of its convex part. Combined with a profile decomposition under integer translations, this principle yields a positive ground state for every rank of the quadratic form. When the periodic potential vanishes, we prove a sharp anisotropic logarithmic Sobolev inequality, determine its optimal constant and all equality cases, and classify positive ground states as explicit anisotropic Gaussons, unique up to translations along the kernel of the quadratic form. When the periodic component is constant, we also establish existence and classify all normalized ground states at every prescribed positive mass, with explicit formulas for the minimum energy and the associated Lagrange multiplier.
item.dc:creator: Baihong Li, Jaros{\l}aw Mederski, Xiangjian Zeng

item.title: The Inviscid Limit in Uniformly Local Yudovich Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.13898v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider solutions to the two-dimensional Navier-Stokes and Euler equations with the velocity in $L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ and the vorticity in the uniformly local Yudovich space $Y^{\theta}_{ul}(\mathbb{R}^2)$. We show that if $\theta$ grows sufficiently slowly, then for every $T>0$, solutions of the Navier-Stokes equation converge to solutions of the Euler equation in $L^{\infty}([0,T];L^2_{ul}(\mathbb{R}^2))$ as $\nu \to 0^+$, provided they are generated from the same initial data.
item.dc:creator: Zachary Radke

item.title: An Aleksandrov estimate for kinetic equations with rough coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.13921v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an exposition of a proof, discovered by Astra, of an Aleksandrov estimate for kinetic equations with rough coefficients. We explain this method in the simpler elliptic and parabolic settings as well.
item.dc:creator: Am\'lie Loher, Connor Mooney, Cl\'ement Mouhot, Lukas Niebel, Luis Silvestre, Yuzhe Zhu

item.title: A Riesz-Map Preconditioned Extragradient Method for Price Formation in Mean Field Games
item.description: arXiv:2610.13934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop and analyze a projected extragradient method, preconditioned by a Riesz map, for a first-order price-formation mean field game in one space dimension. The model couples Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman and transport equations through a global market-clearing constraint. Finite propagation justifies truncating the first-order transport equation to a bounded interval. A monotone weak formulation incorporates the mixed initial--terminal data. Its Riesz map uses $L^2$ norms for density and price directions and a space-time $H^1$ norm for value-function directions, preconditioning the residual without adding higher-order regularization terms to the MFG equations. A density-only argument rules out cocoercivity on the localized admissible set in every equivalent Hilbert metric, motivating extragradient updates. For $H(x,p)=p^2/2$, we use a monotone upwind discretization with adjoint-consistent transport and a state-constraint boundary closure. We establish a mesh-independent Lipschitz bound on bounded convex admissible sets with uniform density, slope, and price bounds. With exact metric projection onto these sets, the iteration converges to a solution of the discrete variational inequality on each fixed grid, with an admissible step-size threshold independent of both mesh sizes. Convergence under mesh refinement is not proved. On a quadratic benchmark, all reported runs reach the stopping tolerance with one fixed step size across a factor-of-16 reduction in both mesh sizes. Price errors and value-function errors measured away from low-density regions decay approximately at first order under refinement, while density errors decrease more slowly.
item.dc:creator: Yeva Gevorgyan, Diogo Gomes

item.title: A higher-dimensional Schr\"odinger maximal estimate along families of bi-Lipschitz curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.12565v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\Theta\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq 1$ be compact with upper Minkowski dimension $\beta$, and let $\gamma(x,t,\theta)$ be a family of curves which is bi-Lipschitz in the first variable and Lipschitz in the last two. We prove the maximal estimate $$\left\|\sup_{(\tau,\theta)\in[0,1)\times\Theta}\left|e^{i\tau\Delta}f(\gamma(\,\cdot\,,\tau,\theta))\right|\right\|_{L^2(B^n_1)}\lesssim_s\|f\|_{H^s(\mathbb{R}^n)},$$ for every $s>\tfrac{n(\beta+1)}{2(n+1)}$, in the range $0\le\beta\le n-1$. In the range $n-1<\beta\leq n$ we prove the threshold $s>\min\big\lbrace\frac\beta 2 + \frac 1{2(n+1)},\frac n2\big\rbrace$. The proof relies on a fractal $L^2$ estimate of Du--Zhang. We also use the temporal localization of Lee, the locally constant property, and a counting argument allowed by the Lipschitz properties of the curve.
item.dc:creator: Javier Minguill\'on

item.title: Sharp lower bound of the first eigenvalue of the $p$-Laplacian under integral Ricci curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.12852v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a sharp Zhong-Yang type lower bound for the first nonzero eigenvalue of the $p$-Laplacian on closed manifolds with small integral Ricci curvature for $p \geq 2$. The proof combines a global elliptic estimate obtained by Sobolev truncation with strict perturbations of one-dimensional comparison profiles.
item.dc:creator: Shoo Seto

item.title: Uniform Exponential Attractors for Non-Autonomous Dynamical Systems and an Application to the damped hyperbolic equation with sub-quintic growth
item.description: arXiv:2610.13068v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we develop an abstract framework for the theory of uniform exponential attractors in non-autonomous dynamical systems. Our construction employs time-dependent absorbing sets while ensuring exponential attraction among the constructed sets. Moreover, we show that the resulting exponential attractors are uniform-that is, they remain stable under perturbations. As an application of this abstract theory, we study the weakly damped hyperbolic equation with sub-quintic nonlinearity. Using the proposed approach, we construct exponential attractors for the process generated by the Shatah-Struwe solution, which satisfies both energy and Strichartz estimates. Furthermore, we establish the Holder continuity of these exponential attractors with respect to the external forcing term.
item.dc:creator: Chang Qingquan, Li Dandan

item.title: Existence of ergodic invariant measures for 3D Navier-Stokes eqs with superlinear noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.13266v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the Navier-Stokes equations in a smooth bounded domain $D\subset \mathbb R^3$. It has been proved in arXiv:2609.08284 that these equations have a unique solution - globally defined in time - when a superlinear noise is introduced and the initial velocity belongs to the space $V$ of divergence-free $H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^3)$-vector fields. Here we show that the same result holds when there is also an additive noise and a deterministic forcing term. Moreover, when the deterministic forcing term is time-independent we prove the existence of at least one invariant measure for this stochastic equation. This is obtained by the Krylov-Bogoliubov method, based on tightness and Feller property in $V$. Finally, we show that the set of invariant measures contains one ergodic invariant measure.
item.dc:creator: Zdzislaw Brzezniak, Benedetta Ferrario, Margherita Zanella

item.title: Recovering a Riemannian manifold from minimal surface areas
item.description: arXiv:2610.13405v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the recovery of a three-dimensional Riemannian manifold from the areas of minimal surfaces. We show that areas of minimal surfaces determine the metric on manifolds foliated by minimal surfaces, up to boundary-fixing isometry. This resolves the conjecture on boundary rigidity for least-area data in an exterior formulation, even without topological restrictions on the minimal surfaces. We also prove global rigidity for Einstein metrics on compact three-manifolds with boundary, assuming $\(\pi_1(M,\partial M)=0\)$ and a non-trapping condition. The Einstein result includes the
item.dc:creator: Catalin Carstea, Matti Lassas, Tony Liimatainen, Leo Tzou

item.title: The binormal flow: a toy model for turbulence
item.description: arXiv:2610.13457v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: These notes summarize the content of a one-week course given by Luis Vega on the binormal flow model applied to describe the dynamics of three-dimensional vortex filaments in incompressible fluids following the Euler equations. This topic touches connections between the binormal flow, the Schr\"odinger map and the 1d cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation, providing a rich casuistry linked to the physical and numerical phenomenology. This course was part of the $2^{\text{nd}}$ Advanced Summer School held at the Institut d'Etudes Scientifiques de Carg\`ese (IESC), at Carg\`ese (Corsica), from $20^{\text{th}}$ to $30^{\text{th}}$ June 2023. These notes have been written and completed by two of its attendees, Elena Danesi and Pablo Merino.
item.dc:creator: Elena Danesi, Pablo Merino, Luis Vega

item.title: Non-resonant angles in a Robin eigenvalue problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.13601v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In an earlier study of the Laplacian eigenvalues with strongly attractive Robin boundary conditions in polygons it was found that if each corner is either concave or non-resonant, then the asymptotic behavior of the individual eigenvalues is determined by an effective one-dimensional operator on the boundary with Dirichlet boundary conditions at the corners. The non-resonance condition was formulated in terms of an eigenvalue bound on truncated sectors, and it was only shown to be satisfied by the right and obtuse opening angles. In the present work, we determine the full range of non-resonant angles: it turns out that the non-resonance condition fails only for the opening angles $\frac{\pi}{2n+1}$ with $n=1,2,3,\dots$, and these critical values are equivalently characterized in terms of the jumps of the eigenvalue counting function and the existence of bounded generalized eigenfunctions. This resolves the numerically supported conjecture stated by Dauge and Lafranche.
item.dc:creator: Konstantin Pankrashkin

item.title: Statistical inference for rough Burgers-type stochastic partial differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.13673v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the Burgers-type stochastic PDE \[ du = \theta\,\partial_x^2 u\,dt + f(u)\,dt + g(u)\,\partial_x u\,dt + \sigma\,dW(t), \] driven by space--time white noise on the one-dimensional torus, where \(\theta>0\) is the diffusivity parameter and \(\sigma>0\) the noise intensity. The transport term \(g(u)\,\partial_x u\) admits no classical interpretation, and we work with the mild solutions defined via rough paths following~\cite{Hairer2011}, for which the solution decomposes as \(u=\psi+R\) with \(\psi\) a stationary centred Gaussian process solving a damped stochastic heat equation and \(R\) a remainder. We first show that, away from the initial time, \(R\) is Lipschitz in space and H\"older in time of order strictly greater than \(1/2\), hence strictly smoother than \(\psi\) in both variables. We then compute exactly the spatial quadratic variation and the temporal quartic variation of \(\psi\), almost surely and not merely in \(L^{2}(\Omega)\), and prove that the corresponding variations of \(u\) are unaffected by the remainder. Combined with an exact time-scaling identity, this separation of regularity scales yields strongly consistent pathwise estimators of \(\theta\). To our knowledge this is the first inference procedure for an SPDE whose solution is defined only pathwise, as a measurable function of a rough path, rather than as an It\^o process.
item.dc:creator: Simon Chony Acosta Christian Olivera Ciprian Tudor

item.title: Sharp upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues on warped products
item.description: arXiv:2610.13738v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We obtain sharp isoperimetric-type upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues on warped products whose bases are compact Riemannian manifolds with boundary and whose fibres are closed Riemannian manifolds. These bounds involve the volume of the warped product and of its boundary, as well as the eigenvalues of the Laplace operator on the fibre and the Steklov eigenvalues of the base. After separation of variables, these bounds are obtained by comparison with auxiliary Helmholtz-Steklov problems on the base involving weighted Laplace operators naturally induced by the warping function. We also study the effect of various natural geometric constraints, such as the warping function being identically equal to one on the boundary. The proofs make use of various spectral approximation methods, including homogenisation on manifolds when the fibres are one-dimensional.
item.dc:creator: Jade Brisson, Bruno Colbois, Alexandre Girouard, Katie Gittins, Jean Lagac\'e-Taylor

item.title: Topping's conjecture for solutions of harmonic map flow with isolated bubbles
item.description: arXiv:2610.13746v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: By establishing a weighted Lojasiewicz-Simon inequality for maps which are close to a fixed harmonic map modulo scaling, we prove Topping's conjecture on continuity of the body map in the case of finite time singularities at which only isolated bubbles form.
item.dc:creator: Melanie Rupflin, Alex Waldron, Sebastian Woodward

item.title: Characterizing higher-dimensional H\"older domains via spherical geometric functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.13866v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we characterize the regularity of a domain in terms of the behavior of a certain spherical function. More precisely, given two domains we show that a certain spherical spectral function (first defined in \cite{FTV23}, see also \cite{AKN21}) has H\"older decay if and only if the domains are complementary and separated by a $C^{1,\beta}$-manifold. This extends the analysis in \cite{Ca24} to dimensions $\geq 3$ and in \cite{FTV23, CTV25} to regularity above the continuous threshold. Along the way, we introduce a spherical analogue of the Jones $\beta$-numbers and show that the decay of these numbers implies geometric regularity of the domain on which they are defined. We believe this result is of independent interest and partially addresses a question of Fleschler-Tolsa-Villa \cite[Question 1]{FTV23}.
item.dc:creator: Emily Casey, Max Engelstein, Tatiana Toro

item.title: The Bernstein problem in higher dimensional Heisenberg groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.13913v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In every sub-Riemannian Heisenberg group $\mathbb H^n$, with $n\geq 2$, we prove the existence of a global perimeter minimizer whose boundary is a smooth, non-characteristic, entire intrinsic graph but it is not a vertical hyperplane.
item.dc:creator: Gianmarco Giovannardi, Simone Verzellesi

item.title: Global higher integrability and Hardy inequalities for double-phase functionals under a capacity density condition
item.description: arXiv:2503.21580v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove global higher integrability for functionals of double-phase type under a uniform local capacity density condition on the complement of the considered domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$. In this context, we investigate a new natural notion of variational capacity associated to the double-phase integrand. Under the related fatness condition for the complement of $\Omega$, we establish an integral Hardy inequality. Further, we show that fatness of $\mathbb{R}^n \setminus \Omega$ is equivalent to a boundary Poincar\'e inequality, a pointwise Hardy inequality and to the local uniform $p$-fatness of $\mathbb{R}^n \setminus \Omega$. We provide a counterexample that shows that the expected Maz'ya type inequality - a key intermediate step toward global higher integrability - does not hold with the notion of capacity involving the double-phase functional itself.
item.dc:creator: Fabian B\"auerlein, Leah Kurki Sch\"atzler, Samuele Ricc\`o

item.title: Modulus of continuity for solutions of non-local heat equations
item.description: arXiv:2507.19023v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend the two-point modulus-of-continuity method for parabolic equations---as used, for instance, in the proof of the fundamental gap conjecture---to non-local heat equations on $\R^n$. An initial modulus of continuity is shown to be preserved provided that its odd extension is a supersolution of an associated one-dimensional non-local equation. The result applies to both integrable and singular kernels, including the fractional Laplacian, and the method further applies to a class of nonlinear non-local heat equations on $\R^n$. We also examine the corresponding regional problem on bounded convex sets. The natural distance-only modulus comparison fails: a smooth counterexample is constructed in one dimension, and the same obstruction is demonstrated to persist in higher dimensions. For the regional fractional Laplacian, we define convex domains of fixed diameter for which the first non-trivial eigenvalue tends to zero. There is consequently no positive Payne--Weinberger-type lower bound for this eigenvalue depending only on the diameter of the domain.
item.dc:creator: Ben Andrews, Sophie Chen

item.title: Long time behavior of discrete velocity kinetic equations
item.description: arXiv:2508.03646v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study long time behavior of some nonlinear discrete velocity kinetic equations in the one and three dimensions with periodic boundary conditions. We prove the exponential time decay of solutions towards the global equilibrium in the $L^2$ space. Our result holds for a wide class of interaction rates including the Goldstein-Taylor and Carleman equations, and the estimates on the rate of convergence are explicit and constructive. The technique is based on the construction of suitable Lyapunov functionals by modifying Boltzmann's entropy.
item.dc:creator: Gayrat Toshpulatov

item.title: Stochastic perturbation and zero noise limit for scalar conservation laws
item.description: arXiv:2510.24475v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Scalar conservation laws sit at the intersection between being simple enough to study analytically, while being complex enough to exhibit a wide range of nonlinear phenomena. We introduce a novel stochastic perturbation of scalar conservation laws, inspired by mean field games. We prove well-posedness of the stochastically perturbed equation; prove that it converges as the noise parameter is sent to $0$; and that the limit is the unique entropy solution of the conservation law. Thus, the noise acts as a selection criterion for (deterministic) conservation laws. This is the first such result for nonlinear hyperbolic conservation laws.
item.dc:creator: Ulrik S. Fjordholm, Magnus C. {\O}rke

item.title: Bubbling analysis of bimeron configurations
item.description: arXiv:2512.11400v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Chiral symmetry breaking in magnetic thin films stabilizes new families of topological solitons that are absent in conventional anisotropic ferromagnets. Beyond the classical chiral skyrmion, which arises in uniaxial systems through the Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interaction, dipolar configurations known as chiral bimerons emerge in easy--plane situations. On compact domains, these solitonic states appear as localized concentrations of energy embedded in an easy--plane background. The analysis, inspired by the Sacks--Uhlenbeck theory for approximate harmonic maps, combines blow--up methods with quantitative rigidity for the M\"obius group to describe the structure, scaling behaviour, and asymptotic limits of such magnetic solitons in both the conformal and large--domain regimes.
item.dc:creator: Glal Bacho, Christof Melcher

item.title: Global Regularity for Non-resistive or Non-viscous MHD System on the Torus
item.description: arXiv:2602.04293v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we establish the global well-posedness of the incompressible magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) system on $n-$dimensional $(n\geq 2)$ periodic boxes with either no magnetic diffusivity (non-resistive case) or no fluid viscosity (non-viscous case) under assumption that initial magnetic fields are sufficiently close to the background magnetic field ${\bf e}_n=(0,\cdots,0,1)$. In Eulerian coordinates, we develop novel time-weighted energy estimates and commutator estimates involving Riesz transforms in negative Sobolev spaces to handle two distinct dissipation cases under different initial symmetry assumptions. The analysis becomes much more difficult and delicate in three- or higher-dimensional cases. In particular, for the three-dimensional and non-resistive case, compared with the regularity requirement proposed by Pan, Zhou and Zhu {\it [Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 2018]}, our result relaxes it from $H^{11}(\mathbb{T}^3)$ to $H^{\frac{9}{2}+}(\mathbb{T}^3)$. And we further establish precise decay rates and growth bounds for both $u(t)$ and $\partial_n(u(t),b(t))$ in Sobolev norms. For the three-dimensional and non-viscous case, we prove the first nonlinear stability result near the background field $\mathbf{e}_3 = (0,0,1)$. This sharply contrasts with the recent blow-up results on the 3D incompressible Euler equations by Elgindi {\it [Ann. Math. 2021]}, Chen-Hou {\it [Commun. Math. Phys. 2021]} and by Chen-Hou {\it [arXiv:2210.07191]}. Our results show that, under certain symmetry assumptions, magnetic fields near the background field provide enhanced dissipations and suppress potential blow-up mechanisms in non-viscous MHD system.
item.dc:creator: Quansen Jiu, Yaowei Xie, Zhihong Yan

item.title: Optimal energy decay rates for Klein-Gordon equations with Kelvin-Voigt damping
item.description: arXiv:2603.26274v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the long-time behaviour of solutions to a one-dimensional linear Klein-Gordon equation with Kelvin-Voigt damping. One of the interesting features of the equation is that the generator of the associated $C_0$-semigroup has multiple spectral points on the imaginary axis. As our main result, we show that the energy of every possible solution converges to zero as time goes to infinity and, moreover, we provide an optimal polynomial energy decay rate for a certain class of solutions.
item.dc:creator: Filippo Dell'Oro, Lassi Paunonen, David Seifert

item.title: Nonlocal Characterizations of Stochastic Completeness on Complete Riemannian Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2604.20205v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we first prove that the following generalized conservation principle holds on complete Riemannian manifolds: for every \(0<s<1\) and \(t>0\), \[ T_t^{(s)}\mathbf 1+\int_0^t T_\tau^{(s)}\mathcal R_s\,d\tau=1 \qquad\text{on }M, \] where \(\mathcal R_s\) is the intrinsic killing term measuring the loss of mass of the subordinate semigroup, and the condition \(\mathcal R_s\equiv0\) is equivalent to the stochastic completeness of \(M\). We then provide several new nonlocal characterizations of stochastic completeness. In particular, we show that stochastic completeness is equivalent to genuinely nonlocal conditions, including the zero-mean identity \[ \int_M (-\Delta)^s\varphi\,dV_g=0 \qquad\forall\,\varphi\in C_c^\infty(M), \] as well as the uniqueness of bounded distributional solutions to the associated fractional elliptic and parabolic equations. We also revisit the equivalent \(L^1\)-core characterization for the generator of the heat semigroup, which plays an important role in our approach. In addition, we prove \(L^p\)-contractivity and smoothing properties of the subordinate semigroup, establish both short-time and long-time asymptotic results for the fractional heat kernel, derive the short-time asymptotics of jump probabilities for the associated Markov process, and study the variational characterization and minimality properties of the fractional resolvent. Together, these results provide a unified analytic and probabilistic framework for the fractional Laplacian on complete Riemannian manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Rui Chen, Bobo Hua

item.title: Leak localisation with a measure source convection-diffusion model
item.description: arXiv:2605.12095v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Taking a variational approach, study the inverse problem of locating gas leaks from line-of-sight concentration measurements using a convection--diffusion model with the source term a Radon measure. By imposing sparsity-promoting regularisation on this measure, we recover point sources---identifying both their locations and intensities---rather than diffuse approximations. We jointly estimate the underlying physical convection (wind) and diffusion parameters. Our main theoretical contribution is the analysis of Lipschitz dependence of the forward solution of the convection--diffusion equation with respect to its parameters: the measure, and the convection and diffusion fields. Numerically, we employ a semi-grid-free optimisation approach for reconstructing the source measure. Our experiments demonstrate accurate localisation, highlighting the potential of the method for practical gas emission detection.
item.dc:creator: Thi Tam Dang, Tuomo Valkonen

item.title: Geometry of the Atomic Condition
item.description: arXiv:2607.22782v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The class AC of integrands satisfying the atomic condition was introduced by De Philippis, De Rosa, and Ghiraldin in 2018. These integrands give rise to Almgren elliptic geometric functionals as proven by the second author and De Rosa in 2020. Explicit examples in intermediate dimensions include small class 2 perturbations of the area integrand and the recent anisotropies constructed by De Rosa, Firester, and Tsiamis, among them the $\ell^q$ norms in Pl\"ucker coordinates for $q$ close to $2$. We reinterpret the atomic condition in terms of convex geometry. We also propose variants of AC, related to the SAC and USAC defined by De Rosa and Tione, which we call the exposed condition EC, the strong exposed condition SEC, and the quadratic exposed condition QEC. For integrands of class 2, QEC is equivalent to validity of a Caccioppoli-type inequality and is stable under class 2 perturbations; every such QEC integrand admits Lipschitzian normals. Combining these results with a result of De Rosa, Firester, and Tsiamis, we prove that a Lipschitz graph whose anisotropic mean curvature for a QEC integrand of class 2 is $p$-integrable, with $k < p < \infty$, is of class $\mathscr{C}^{1,\alpha}$ on an open set of full measure. Finally, for all $k \ge 2$ and $n - k \ge 3$ we construct strictly polyconvex integrands - associated to inner-product norms on $\bigwedge_k \mathbf{R}^n$ - which fail the atomic condition, showing that strict polyconvexity is necessary but not sufficient for AC.
item.dc:creator: Jacek Jakimiuk, S{\l}awomir Kolasi\'nski, Maciej Le\'sniak

item.title: Tangent-cone cancellation and Maz'ya's $\Phi$-inequalities on finitely cornered planar domains
item.description: arXiv:2609.12755v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $0<\alpha<2$ and $p=2/(2-\alpha)$. We study critical nonlinear convolution inequalities for kernels $K:\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\}\to\mathbb{R}^m$ and functions $\Phi:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}$ positively homogeneous of degrees $\alpha-2$ and $p$. We assume angular Lipschitz regularity for $\Phi$ and angular $C^{0,\gamma}$ regularity for $K$, where $0<\gamma\le1$ and $\gamma=1$ if $p<2$. On bounded finitely cornered planar domains with a common Dini tangent modulus on the boundary branches, we characterize $|\int_\Omega\Phi(K*f) dx|\le C\|f\|_{L^1}^p$ for real densities $f\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)\cap L^s_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^2)$, $1<s\le\infty$, by signed angular cancellation on the plane, tangent half-planes, and full vertex tangent cones. An analogous criterion holds on infinite sectors for compactly supported mean-zero densities. For the Newton kernel and each nonzero angularly Lipschitz, positively two-homogeneous $\Phi:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}$ with vanishing half-circle moments, we construct a bounded convex $C^1$ domain $\Omega_\Phi$, independent of $\varepsilon$, and smooth tests $u_\varepsilon$ satisfying $\|\Delta u_\varepsilon\|_{L^1(\Omega_\Phi)}+\|\partial_nu_\varepsilon\|_{L^1(\partial\Omega_\Phi)}\le2$, while, despite tangent cancellation, their nonlinear integrals grow in magnitude like $\log\log(1/\varepsilon)$. On the Dini class, a constant-preserving linear extension with compact support modulo the domain mean and controlled measure-valued Laplacian yields the same necessary-and-sufficient criterion for the Newton-kernel PDE inequality, without exact corner charts. We also construct infinite-dimensional cancellation spaces containing nonquadratic functions and classify the quadratic locus in polygon moduli.
item.dc:creator: Zhouyu Long, Wenming Zou

item.title: Oblique boundary value problems for n-1type augmented Hessian equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.11400v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the global regularity of oblique boundary value problems for n-1 type augmented Hessian equations on a bounded domain, without imposing any convexity condition either on the domain or on the matrix-valued function in the n-1 type augmented Hessian equations. We establish a global existence and uniqueness theory for classical elliptic solutions by deriving global a priori estimates up to second-order derivatives. Besides the known applications for n-1 type Monge-Ampere operators in optimal transportation and geometric optics, the general theory here embraces equations raised by Li-Sheng, Some Dirichlet problems arising from conformal geometry. Pac. J. Math. 251, 2011, 337-359 and Guan-Qiu-Yuan, Fully nonlinear elliptic equations for conformal deformations of Chern-Ricci forms. Adv. Math. 343, 2019, 538-566.
item.dc:creator: Zhibo Hu, Feida Jiang

item.title: Pointwise Structures and Background Perturbation Analyses for Thermal Non-equilibrium Irrotational Flows in Three Space Dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.11676v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, both the pointwise space-time structures of the solution for a three-dimensional model describing gas dynamics in thermal non-equilibrium and the corresponding background stabilities within the $L^p$ framework are investigated under the small initial perturbation assumption and the irrotationality condition. Our main tools are the modified Green's function according to the irrotationality condition, a priori energy method and a refined decay estimates of products composed of the entropy function and high-order derivatives.
item.dc:creator: Shijin Deng, Xiaochun Yang

item.title: (In)finiteness of slopes for Monge-Amp\`ere equations at flat boundary pieces
item.description: arXiv:2610.12165v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: On any bounded convex domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ with a $d$-dimensional flat boundary piece $F\subset\partial\Omega$, we consider convex solutions with zero boundary values to the Monge-Amp\`ere equations $$ \det\mathsf{D}^2 u= \mathrm{dist}(\,\cdot\,,\mathrm{Aff}(F))^\alpha,\quad\det\mathsf{D}^2 u=\mathrm{dist}(\,\cdot\,,\partial\Omega)^\alpha,\quad \det\mathsf{D}^2 u=(-u)^\alpha, $$ where $\mathrm{dist}$ stands for Euclidean distance and $\mathrm{Aff}(F)$ is the affine hull of $F$. We show that the threshold of the exponent $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$ for $u$ to have infinite slope at $F$ is $\alpha\leq 2d-n$. For the first two equations, we also show that no solution exists when $\alpha\leq 2d-2n$. Moreover, when $\Omega$ satisfies the ``exterior cone condition with a $d$-dimensional ridge'' at $F$, both thresholds are sharp for the first equation, and the infinite-slope threshold is sharp for the last equation.
item.dc:creator: Xin Nie

item.title: Improved fractal Weyl bounds for convex cocompact hyperbolic surfaces and large resonance-free regions
item.description: arXiv:2301.03023v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $X$ be a convex cocompact hyperbolic surface, and let $\delta$ denote the Hausdorff dimension of its limit set. Let $N_X(\sigma,T)$ denote the number of resonances of $X$ inside the box $[\sigma, \delta] + i[0,T]$. We prove that for all $\sigma > \delta/2$, we have \[ N_X(\sigma,T) \ll_\epsilon T^{1 + \delta - 2(2\sigma - \delta) + \epsilon}. \] This strengthens the previously established "improved" fractal Weyl bounds due to Naud \cite{Naud14} and Dyatlov \cite{Dya19}. Moreover, this result implies that for every $\epsilon > 0$, there exist resonance-free rectangular boxes of arbitrary height within the strip \[ \left\{\, s \in \mathbb{C} : \tfrac{3}{4}\delta + \epsilon < \mathrm{Re}(s) < \delta\, \right\}. \] Our proof combines Naud's approach \cite{Naud14} with the refined transfer operator machinery developed by Dyatlov-Zworski \cite{DyZw18}, as well as a new estimate for oscillatory integrals that arise naturally in our analysis.
item.dc:creator: Louis Soares

item.title: Lojasiewicz inequalities for maps of the 2-sphere
item.description: arXiv:2312.16686v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a Lojasiewicz-Simon inequality $$ \left| E(u) - 4\pi n \right| \leq C \| \mathcal{T}(u) \|^\alpha $$ for maps $u \in W^{2,2}\left( S^2, S^2 \right).$ The inequality holds with $\alpha = 1$ in general and with $\alpha > 1$ unless $u$ is nearly constant on an open set. We obtain polynomial convergence of weak solutions of harmonic map flow $u(t) : S^2 \to S^2$ as $t \to \infty$ on compact domains away from the singular set, assuming that the body map is nonconstant.
